summary.text: Jessica Ramos is a member of the New York State Senate representing District 13, which includes Corona, Elmhurst, East Elmhurst and Jackson Heights in Queens, and she assumed office on January 1, 2019.
Wikipedia says she chairs the Senate Labor Committee, ran for New York City mayor in 2025, and lost the 2026 Democratic primary for her Senate seat to Jessica González-Rojas.

paragraphs.text: Wikipedia says Ramos was born at Elmhurst Hospital and raised in Astoria, the daughter of Colombian immigrants, and attended Hofstra University without completing a degree.
She worked in New York City Hall as a communications adviser and later director of Latino media from April 2016 to December 2017, and earlier was communications director for Build Up NYC.
She served on Queens Community Board 3 and was a Queens County Democratic district leader from 2010 to 2014.
Ramos challenged Senator Jose Peralta in the 2018 Democratic primary and won the seat, according to Wikipedia, and she has chaired the Labor Committee since entering the Senate.
Wikipedia says she began a campaign for mayor in September 2024, endorsed Andrew Cuomo in June 2025 while remaining on the ballot, and placed ninth in the first round of ranked-choice voting.
Ballotpedia lists her current term as ending on January 1, 2027.
